item.title: Re: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Dr Elliot Anemone. Apologies for the delay in getting this critique to you. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ crit
- crit

While the idea sounds interesting, and the new, proposed GoI has potential, I feel your Central Narrative has a couple of convenient conjectures that don’t really hold up to scrutiny. I’ll list a couple below for you to iron out:

after something interfered with the communications between the foundation and the agents

What interfered with the communications? Is this crucial to the story, or simply a way for you (the author) to get the MTF captured? Speaking of being captured, what happens to the MTF? You quickly go into another set of Foundation agents who discover the scp – why not simply start your discovery log at this point? Was there a need for the MTF to go in first?

Doctor Josef Monstrosity thanking the foundation for finding their med students projects, and left this one as a show of thanks.

Why would this gesture be “a show of thanks”?

attempts by the Foundation to gain the Fishmans trust in hopes that it is capable of telling the Foundation where it came from

If it were experimented on by the medical students, wouldn’t the Fishman automatically side with the Foundation? Why the resistance to give up a place and people who tortured it?

Dr. Franklin, a young researcher with vague origins, but was brought in by the higher ups so staff just decide it's best not to question it

Again, this sounds dubious at best, unprofessional at worst. You’ve introduced a character to advance the story, and nothing else. There’s no reason for his inclusion at this point unless you have a good explanation for his appearance.

how it went to the hospital willingly at first because when it was human it had aquagenic urticaria and the hospital said they could cure him

This is a good motivation for the scip to have, and an excellent introduction to what the new GoI is capable / not capable of doing. The problem is you seem to have given us conflicting views of what the GoI actually is: is it a place for so-called monsters to go to get cured or experimented on?

how the Hospital views normalcy as an illness that needs to be remedied.

This, then, becomes even more problematic as you have an additional goal for the GoI. Why was it experimenting on the fish-man then? Wouldn’t it view all mutants as normal people?

Lots of plot inconsistencies I hope you can help clear up. If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: Re: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)
item.content:encoded:
Hey, I'm here upon request so lets take a look at what you got goin on.

Taking a look at the anomaly itself, it seems like it has the potential to be fairly interesting but isn't quite there. So far I see some sort of fish monster that was made, and it doesn't seem to go much further than that. Like said above, you give quite a bit on how it was found/came to but not real much on what happens with it afterwards. Infact, you kind of deflate the possibilities by limiting the SCP to be "rabid", which seems like a broad term and one you should avoid. Give some depth to the SCP, humanoid SCPs are usually interesting because they can communicate and express emotion. It seems this has the ability to do neither, and no opportunity to gain that ability. So for the SCP, I'd suggest to narrow it down to a more concise and focused object that allows for some depth and post containment development. I would also suggest rewriting the part of the SCP just being a kill monster, perhaps narrow down what triggers it instincts of flight/fight.

As for the story, I'll agree with cybersqyd on this one and say I'm rather confused on why the doctor needs to be so mysterious. You imply there are sinister things at work,but how do we know all this about the doctor, and how did he manage to infiltrate the Foundation? Is this GOI notable? Or is it the first appearance of them? You should also detail a bit of what you'd like to do with the story post containment. The whole infiltration plot seems like it can hold steam, but does the SCP actually have the ability to talk? And how are we finding out about the plot? Through an investigation? or perhaps a journal of the doctor left behind? I would examine these parts and narrow down the story some so that it flows better, and has a focus to it. Best of luck.

item.title: Re: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

a feral humanoid fish with the traits of multiple types of marine life that has a fear of Doctors.

What kinda fish traits are we looking at here?

The SCP is one of multiple anomalous entities that were found by Foundation MTF agents that mentioned something about a hospital that hurt them, but after something interfered with the communications between the foundation and the agents, the other entities and MTF agents were taken captive by an unknown threat. the SCP was found by another group of Foundation agents who found it unconscious and injured, along with a note from a Doctor Josef Monstrosity thanking the foundation for finding their med students projects, and left this one as a show of thanks.

I'm a little uncertain as to how all this would be shown: like, the first part feels like it'd be vague communications and not really like, something fully in the article? And the second part feels…fine but like it has weird implications around this doctor that don't really go anywhere?

I think, at the end of the day, my biggest concern is that it feels too much like the focus of the narrative is on 'how did we find this thing' when to me the most interesting question is about what happens now it's contained: the fear of doctors and strange fishy nature feels like it'd give a lot of room for exploring how the foundation interacts with this, while the Dr Josef Monstrosity angle feels like it'd give a lot of room for exploring his role in this whole thing and like, what his existence means for the broader world.

It also feels like the narrative is very divorced from the actual scp: like my general rule of thumb is that if you could swap the scp object out for something with completely different properties, then the narrative is probably too broadly focussed.

item.title: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)
item.content:encoded:
a carnivorous humanoid fish that was the victim of horrible experiments by an unknown organization.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: a humanoid fish with the traits of multiple types of marine life, such as bio-luminescence, the ability to generate electricity like an electric eel, but can generate up to 50,000 volts of electricity, and shark-like teeth that can bite through reinforced iron. The SCP also has a fear of Doctors.

Central Narrative: The SCP is one of multiple anomalous entities that were found by Foundation MTF agents that mentioned something about a place called Monstrosity Hospital, a GOI that the Foundation hadn't encountered before, but after something interfered with the communications between the foundation and the agents, the other entities and MTF agents were taken captive by representatives of Monstrosity Hospital. the SCP was found by another group of Foundation agents who found it unconscious and injured, along with a note from a Doctor Josef Monstrosity thanking the foundation for finding their med students projects, and left this one as a show of thanks. most of the tests with this SCP is attempts by the Foundation to gain the Fishmans trust in hopes that it is capable of telling the Foundation where it came from, and the only doctor who's made any progress in the area is Dr. Franklin, a young researcher with vague origins, but was brought in by the higher ups so staff just decide it's best not to question it, though Dr. Franklin claims that the Fish-man is just an animal and is too stupid to understand anything beyond basic instinct. eventually it's found out through an investigation that Dr. Franklin is from Monstrosity Hospital and is in fact the same med-student that created the Fish-man in the first place, sent here to keep the Fish-man quiet, as well as get information on the Foundation. After Dr. Franklin is terminated by the Foundation, the SCP reveals that it can talk, but was under threat by Dr. Franklin to not speak a word to Foundation staff. the SCP then goes on to become a source of information about this new GOI, Monstrosity Hospital, saying things like how it went to the hospital willingly at first because when it was human it had aquagenic urticaria and the hospital said they could cure him, and how the Hospital views normalcy as an illness that needs to be remedied.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the SCP shows strong signs of human DNA and has even said that it was a human once. the SCP gets it's name because it wears a green hospital band on its wrist that has "Med Student Freddy" written where the doctors name would be. It also possesses a severe case of iatrophobia (the fear of doctors for anyone who didn't know that), to the point that just the sight of someone wearing a lab coat can cause the SCP to go into a state of extreme panic, which is why researchers are instructed not to wear lab coats when they enter the SCPs containment cell.

Additional Notes:I hope this is a step in the right direction.
